domiati.name: Domiati
domiati.summary: Soft, salty white cheese made mainly in Egypt from buffalo, cow, or mixed milk, and named after the port city of Damietta; Egypt's most common cheese.

kerma-culture.name: Kerma culture
kerma-culture.summary: An early civilization and kingdom in ancient Nubia, in what is now Sudan, flourishing from about 2500 to 1500 BCE and rivaling Egypt before Egypt's New Kingdom absorbed it.

herodotus.name: Herodotus
herodotus.summary: Greek historian and geographer (c. 484–c. 425 BC), called 'the Father of History' for his Histories, a detailed account of the Greco-Persian Wars and the peoples and lands around them.

sneferu.name: Sneferu
sneferu.summary: First pharaoh of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty, around 2600 BC, who introduced major innovations in pyramid design and construction.

khufu.name: Khufu
khufu.summary: Second pharaoh of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty, reigning in the 26th century BC, credited with commissioning the Great Pyramid of Giza.

abydos-egypt.name: Abydos
abydos-egypt.summary: One of ancient Egypt's oldest cities, home to a royal necropolis of early pharaohs and the memorial temple of Seti I.

fifth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: Fifth Dynasty of Egypt
fifth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: A line of pharaohs who ruled Egypt's Old Kingdom for about 150 years, from the early 25th to mid-24th century BC.

userkaf.name: Userkaf
userkaf.summary: The founder of ancient Egypt's Fifth Dynasty, reigning in the early 25th century BC, whose rule marked the rise of the sun god Ra's cult as Egypt's state religion.

fourth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: Fourth Dynasty
fourth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: A 'golden age' of ancient Egypt's Old Kingdom, lasting from about 2613 to 2498 BC and marked by peace, prosperity, and the height of pyramid building.

abusir.name: Abusir
abusir.summary: Ancient Egyptian pyramid site near Memphis with four Old Kingdom kings' pyramids, part of a UNESCO World Heritage necropolis.

lower-nubia.name: Lower Nubia
lower-nubia.summary: Northernmost part of ancient Nubia, now largely submerged under Lake Nasser after the Aswan High Dam's construction, with its monuments relocated in a major 20th-century rescue effort.

middle-kingdom-of-egypt.name: Middle Kingdom of Egypt
middle-kingdom-of-egypt.summary: A period of ancient Egyptian history, about 2040 to 1782 or 1700 BC, following reunification under Mentuhotep II, when Osiris became the leading popular deity.

khafre.name: Khafre
khafre.summary: An ancient Egyptian king of the Fourth Dynasty (died c. 2532 BC), son of Khufu, whose pyramid at Giza is second only in size to his father's.

djedefre.name: Djedefre
djedefre.summary: Ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the 4th Dynasty, son and successor of Khufu, who introduced the royal title 'Son of Ra' linking kings to the sun god.

twelfth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: Twelfth Dynasty
twelfth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: A line of Egyptian pharaohs ruling from about 1991 to 1802 BCE, considered the peak of the Middle Kingdom, running from Amenemhat I to Sobekneferu.

semna-nubia.name: Semna
semna-nubia.summary: A fortified area on the Nile in Lower Nubia, established under Pharaoh Senusret I around 1965 to 1920 BC as part of a chain of Middle Kingdom fortresses guarding Egypt's southern frontier.

uronarti.name: Uronarti
uronarti.summary: An island in the Nile in northern Sudan holding one of several Middle Kingdom Egyptian fortresses built in Nubia, now largely submerged under Lake Nasser.

senusret-iii.name: Senusret III
senusret-iii.summary: Fifth king of Egypt's late 12th Dynasty, whose campaigns brought an era of peace and prosperity; he was one of the few Egyptian kings worshipped as a god during his own lifetime, dying around 1839 BC.

hyksos.name: Hyksos
hyksos.summary: Kings of Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty, about 1650 to 1550 BCE, likely of Levantine origin, who were the first foreign rulers of Egypt.

khyan.name: Khyan
khyan.summary: A Hyksos king of Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty in the later 17th century BC, known from many seals and objects showing diplomatic contacts as far as Crete, the Hittites and Babylon.

kassites.name: Kassites
kassites.summary: A people from the Zagros Mountains who controlled Babylonia under the Kassite dynasty from about 1531 to 1155 BC, ruling first from Babylon and later from Dur-Kurigalzu.

c-group-culture.name: C-Group culture
c-group-culture.summary: An archaeological culture of Lower Nubia dated about 2400–1550 BCE, named by George Reisner after it left no central site or written records of its people's own name.

khasekhemwy.name: Khasekhemwy
khasekhemwy.summary: The last pharaoh of Egypt's Second Dynasty, around 2690 BC, who led major military campaigns, reunified Egypt by his 13th year, and built the large mudbrick Shunet El Zebib.

hor-aha.name: Hor-Aha
hor-aha.summary: Considered by most Egyptologists the second pharaoh of Egypt's First Dynasty (others say the first), reigning around the 31st century BC for a long period.

eighteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt
eighteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: The first dynasty of Egypt's New Kingdom (1550–1292 BC), the era of Egypt's peak power, including pharaohs Tutankhamun, Hatshepsut and Akhenaten.

mentuhotep-ii.name: Mentuhotep II
mentuhotep-ii.summary: A pharaoh of Egypt's 11th Dynasty who reunited Upper and Lower Egypt after civil war, ending the First Intermediate Period and beginning the Middle Kingdom over a 51-year reign.

kingdom-of-kush.name: Kingdom of Kush
kingdom-of-kush.summary: An ancient kingdom in Nubia along the Nile in what is now Sudan and Egypt, rising from the city-state of Kerma and later ruling Egypt itself in the 8th century BCE under King Piye.

merneptah.name: Merneptah
merneptah.summary: Fourth pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty, reigning for almost ten years from 1213 BC; son of Ramesses II, best known for the stele mentioning Israel.

battle-of-perire.name: Battle of Perire
battle-of-perire.summary: A battle around 1208 BC in which Pharaoh Merneptah's Egyptian forces decisively defeated a coalition of Libyan tribes and Sea Peoples, the first of many such clashes, recorded in the Great Karnak Inscription.

sea-peoples.name: Sea Peoples
sea-peoples.summary: A group of tribes who raided Egypt and other eastern Mediterranean regions around 1200 BC, once seen as a main cause of the Bronze Age collapse but now often viewed as refugees fleeing an ongoing crisis.

great-karnak-inscription.name: Great Karnak Inscription
great-karnak-inscription.summary: A 79-line hieroglyphic inscription at Karnak recording pharaoh Merneptah's campaign against the Sea Peoples at the Battle of Perire; it is the longest surviving continuous monumental text from Egypt.

khopesh.name: Khopesh
khopesh.summary: A sickle-shaped Egyptian sword developed from battle axes, originating in Western Asia during the Bronze Age and introduced to Egypt in the Second Intermediate Period, becoming common in the New Kingdom.

viceroy-of-kush.name: Viceroy of Kush
viceroy-of-kush.summary: The Egyptian official who governed Nubia after its annexation around the 16th century BC, overseeing tribute collection until the title faded from use after Piankh's reign.

meryey.name: Meryey
meryey.summary: A Berber king and Great Chief of the Libu in the late 13th century BC, who organized a military alliance with other Libyan groups and Sea Peoples against pharaoh Merneptah.

meshwesh.name: Meshwesh
meshwesh.summary: An ancient Libyan tribe first recorded under pharaoh Amenhotep III around 1390-1350 BC, later often at war with Egypt and eventually ruling it during the 22nd and 23rd Dynasties.

sherden.name: Sherden
sherden.summary: One of the groups said to make up the Sea Peoples, known from Egyptian and Ugaritic records and distinguished by horned helmets and swords.

shekelesh.name: Shekelesh
shekelesh.summary: One of several groups said to make up the Sea Peoples, known from fragmentary Egyptian records of the late second millennium BCE.

senusret-i.name: Senusret I
senusret-i.summary: Second king of Egypt's 12th Dynasty, son of Amenemhat I, who expanded Egypt's territory and ruled during a prosperous age until his death around 1926 BC.

cataracts-of-the-nile.name: Second Cataract
cataracts-of-the-nile.summary: One of the shallow, rocky stretches of the Nile between Khartoum and Aswan, broken by boulders, islets and rapids.

buhen.name: Buhen
buhen.summary: Ancient Egyptian settlement on the Nile below the Second Cataract in what is now Sudan, founded as an Old Kingdom colonial town known for copper smelting and later fortified as a frontier garrison.

ahmose-son-of-ebana.name: Ahmose, son of Ebana
ahmose-son-of-ebana.summary: Egyptian military officer who served under pharaohs Ahmose I, Amenhotep I and Thutmose I; his tomb autobiography is a key source on the late 17th and early 18th Dynasties.

amenhotep-i.name: Amenhotep I
amenhotep-i.summary: Second pharaoh of Egypt's 18th Dynasty, who ruled about 21 years, maintained his father's conquests, and was later worshipped as a patron god.

thutmose-i.name: Thutmose I
thutmose-i.summary: Third pharaoh of Egypt's 18th Dynasty, reigning around 1506 to 1493 BCE, who extended Egypt's borders into the Levant and Nubia and built the first known royal tomb in the Valley of the Kings.

nineteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: 19th Dynasty
nineteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: The second dynasty of Egypt's New Kingdom, lasting from 1292 to 1189 BC, founded by Ramesses I and part of what is called the Ramesside period.

zawyet-umm-el-rakham.name: Zawyet Umm El Rakham
zawyet-umm-el-rakham.summary: An archaeological site on Egypt's north coast west of Marsa Matruh that was a major fortress-town under Ramesses II, marking the western edge of Egyptian control; discovered in 1948.

ian-shaw-egyptologist.name: Ian Shaw
ian-shaw-egyptologist.summary: A British Egyptologist, born 1961, with a Cambridge PhD, who is a Reader in Egyptian Archaeology at Liverpool and directs archaeological projects in Egypt.

ramesses-ii.name: Ramesses II
ramesses-ii.summary: Third pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty (c. 1303–1213 BC), often called Ramesses the Great; his 66-year reign, the longest of any pharaoh, included 15 military campaigns.

shasu.name: Shasu
shasu.summary: Semitic-speaking pastoral nomads of the Southern Levant from the late Bronze Age into the Iron Age, organized in clans under tribal chieftains and sometimes serving as mercenaries.

moab.name: Moab
moab.summary: An ancient kingdom in what is now southern Jordan, along the Dead Sea, known from the Mesha Stele and often in conflict with its Israelite neighbors.

battle-of-kadesh.name: Battle of Kadesh
battle-of-kadesh.summary: A major c.1274 BCE battle between Ramesses II of Egypt and Muwatalli II of the Hittites, the earliest pitched battle in recorded history with known tactics, ending in stalemate.

horemheb.name: Horemheb
horemheb.summary: Last pharaoh of Egypt's 18th Dynasty, ruling from about 1319 to 1292 BC, who rose from army commander to restabilize the country after the Amarna Period.

old-kingdom-of-egypt.name: Old Kingdom
old-kingdom-of-egypt.summary: An ancient Egyptian period lasting from about 2700 to 2200 BCE, called the Age of the Pyramids for the great pyramid-building kings of the Fourth Dynasty.

richard-b-parkinson.name: Richard B. Parkinson
richard-b-parkinson.summary: British Egyptologist and Oxford professor, formerly a curator of Ancient Egypt and Sudan at the British Museum until 2013.

pyramid-texts.name: Pyramid Texts
pyramid-texts.summary: The oldest known ancient Egyptian funerary texts, carved on pyramid and tomb walls from the late Old Kingdom, dating from about 2400–2300 BCE and reserved for the pharaoh.

egyptian-language.name: Classical Egyptian
egyptian-language.summary: Also known as Middle Egyptian, the classical literary form of the ancient Egyptian language, used as the vernacular of the Middle Kingdom and later as Egypt's literary standard.

new-kingdom-of-egypt.name: New Kingdom of Egypt
new-kingdom-of-egypt.summary: The period of ancient Egypt from about the 16th to 11th century BC, covering the 18th to 20th dynasties, marking Egypt's greatest power and territorial extent.

sebayt.name: Sebayt
sebayt.summary: The ancient Egyptian genre of formally written ethical teachings and instructions on 'the way of living truly,' considered a form of wisdom literature.

ipuwer-papyrus.name: Ipuwer Papyrus
ipuwer-papyrus.summary: An ancient Egyptian papyrus from the Nineteenth Dynasty containing the incomplete literary work Admonitions of Ipuwer, likely composed no earlier than around 1991–1803 BCE.

amenemhat-iii.name: Amenemhat III
amenemhat-iii.summary: Sixth king of Egypt's Twelfth Dynasty, whose reign marked the Middle Kingdom's cultural and economic peak and included major building work around Faiyum.

seth-peribsen.name: Seth-Peribsen
seth-peribsen.summary: Early Egyptian pharaoh of the Second Dynasty (c. 2890-2686 BC) whose reign's length and place among contemporaries are unknown; unusually, his royal name invoked the god Set rather than Horus.

upper-and-lower-egypt.name: The Two Lands
upper-and-lower-egypt.summary: The ancient Egyptian concept of the realm as two united lands, Upper and Lower Egypt, reflected in pharaohs' titles and symbolized by the papyrus and lily plants.

ancient-egyptian-royal-titulary.name: Dual King
ancient-egyptian-royal-titulary.summary: Part of the standard set of five names taken by pharaohs of ancient Egypt, symbolizing royal and divine power; the full titulary became standard usage from the Middle Kingdom onward.

nubia.name: Nubia
nubia.summary: A region along the Nile between Khartoum and Aswan, seat of ancient civilizations including the Kerma culture and the Kingdom of Kush, which conquered Egypt in the 8th century BC.

kerma.name: Kerma
kerma.summary: Capital of the Kingdom of Kerma in present-day Sudan and one of the largest archaeological sites in ancient Nubia. It was first settled by hunter-gatherers around 8350 BC and has thousands of graves and tombs.

western-deffufa.name: Western Deffufa
western-deffufa.summary: Mudbrick temple about 20 meters high in the ancient city of Kerma in northern Sudan, one of the oldest known monumental structures in the Nile Valley. Its chambers and courtyards were probably used for religious rituals.

ancient-egyptian-calendar.name: Egyptian calendar
ancient-egyptian-calendar.summary: A 365-day solar civil calendar used in ancient Egypt, split into three 120-day seasons plus five extra days, which slowly drifted out of step with the true solar year.

edwin-smith-papyrus.name: Edwin Smith Papyrus
edwin-smith-papyrus.summary: Ancient Egyptian medical text, copied around 1600 BCE, considered the oldest known surgical treatise on trauma, describing 48 cases of injuries and wounds.

ebers-papyrus.name: Ebers Papyrus
ebers-papyrus.summary: An Egyptian medical papyrus of herbal knowledge dating to about 1550 BCE, among the oldest and most important medical texts of ancient Egypt.

nilometer.name: Nilometer
nilometer.summary: A structure for measuring the Nile's water level and clarity during its annual flood, used from pharaonic times through the Islamic period until the Aswan Dam made them obsolete in the 1960s.

sopdet.name: Sopdet
sopdet.summary: The Egyptian name for the star Sirius and its personification as a goddess, known to the Greeks as Sothis and linked with Isis.

heliacal-rising.name: Heliacal rising
heliacal-rising.summary: The moment a star or planet becomes visible again above the eastern horizon just before sunrise, after being hidden in the sun's glare; the rising of Sirius was key to the ancient Egyptian calendar.

second-intermediate-period-of-egypt.name: Second Intermediate Period of Egypt
second-intermediate-period-of-egypt.summary: A period from 1782 to 1550 BC when Egypt was again divided into rival dynasties, best known for the Hyksos, who ruled from Avaris after settling in Egypt.

faiyum.name: Faiyum
faiyum.summary: A city in Egypt's Faiyum Oasis, about 100 kilometres southwest of Cairo, and one of the country's oldest cities owing to its strategic location.

book-of-nut.name: Book of Nut
book-of-nut.summary: A collection of ancient Egyptian astronomical texts about the stars, moon, sun and planets, named for the sky goddess Nut who is shown arching over the earth in some copies.

rhind-mathematical-papyrus.name: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus
rhind-mathematical-papyrus.summary: One of two well-known ancient Egyptian mathematical papyri, alongside the Moscow Mathematical Papyrus, copied by the scribe Ahmes and a key source on Egyptian mathematics.

ahmes.name: Ahmes
ahmes.summary: Ancient Egyptian scribe who transcribed the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus around 1550 BC, making him the earliest contributor to mathematics whose name is known.

flinders-petrie.name: Flinders Petrie
flinders-petrie.summary: English Egyptologist and archaeology pioneer (1853–1942) who developed methodical excavation and pottery-based dating techniques and held Britain's first chair in Egyptology.

menes.name: Menes
menes.summary: A pharaoh credited by tradition with uniting Upper and Lower Egypt and founding its First Dynasty around 3100 BC, often identified with the ruler Narmer.

narmer.name: Narmer
narmer.summary: An early Egyptian king around 3100 BC widely considered the unifier of Egypt and founder of its First Dynasty, often identified with the legendary king Menes.

heracleopolis-magna.name: Heracleopolis Magna
heracleopolis-magna.summary: Ancient Egyptian city, capital of the 20th nome of Upper Egypt, located near modern Beni Suef.

pschent.name: Pschent
pschent.summary: The double crown worn by ancient Egyptian pharaohs, combining the white crown of Upper Egypt and red crown of Lower Egypt to represent rule over the unified kingdom.

thutmose-iii.name: Thutmose III
thutmose-iii.summary: Pharaoh of Egypt's 18th Dynasty who ruled from 1479 to 1425 BCE, led 17 to 20 victorious military campaigns, and created Egypt's first navy, earning him the nickname "the Napoleon of Egypt."

amenhotep-iii.name: Amenhotep III
amenhotep-iii.summary: Ninth pharaoh of Egypt's 18th Dynasty, ruling around 1386–1349 BC during a peak of Egyptian wealth and influence; father of Akhenaten.

egyptian-hittite-peace-treaty.name: Egyptian–Hittite peace treaty
egyptian-hittite-peace-treaty.summary: A peace agreement made around 1259 BC between Ramesses II of Egypt and Hittite king Hattusili III, the oldest known surviving peace treaty in history.

pi-ramesses.name: Pi-Ramesses
pi-ramesses.summary: The new capital built by pharaoh Ramesses II at Qantir near the older site of Avaris, having earlier served as a summer palace under Seti I.

tausret.name: Tausret
tausret.summary: Final pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty, who died in 1188 BC; her independent reign lasted roughly two to three years after she assumed her predecessor Siptah's regnal years.

setnakhte.name: Setnakhte
setnakhte.summary: First pharaoh of Egypt's Twentieth Dynasty, ruling 1188 to 1185 BC, and father of Ramesses III.

twentieth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: Twentieth Dynasty
twentieth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: The last dynasty of ancient Egypt's New Kingdom, ruling 1189–1077 BCE, whose reign is generally seen as the start of Egypt's decline amid invasions by the Sea Peoples.

early-dynastic-period-of-egypt.name: Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)
early-dynastic-period-of-egypt.summary: The era of ancient Egypt just after Upper and Lower Egypt were unified around 3150 BC, covering the First and Second Dynasties until about 2686 BC.

seti-ii.name: Seti II
seti-ii.summary: Seti II: Fifth pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty, reigning c. 1203 to 1197 BC, who faced a rival claimant, Amenmesse, who seized control of Thebes and Nubia in Upper Egypt during his second to fourth regnal years.

amenmesse.name: Amenmesse
amenmesse.summary: Fifth pharaoh of Egypt's 19th Dynasty, who ruled only three or four years around 1200 BC and whose parentage is uncertain.

ramesses-iii.name: Ramesses III
ramesses-iii.summary: Second pharaoh of Egypt's Twentieth Dynasty, reigning roughly 1185 to 1154 BC; the last New Kingdom pharaoh with real power, he defeated the Sea Peoples but was later assassinated in a harem conspiracy.

tiye.name: Queen Tiye
tiye.summary: Great Royal Wife of pharaoh Amenhotep III (c. 1398–1338 BC), mother of Akhenaten and grandmother of Tutankhamun; DNA analysis in 2010 confirmed her as the mummy known as 'The Elder Lady.'

pentawer.name: Pentawer
pentawer.summary: An ancient Egyptian prince of the 20th Dynasty, son of Ramesses III, implicated in a plot to kill his father and forced to commit suicide after trial.

ramesses-iv.name: Ramesses IV
ramesses-iv.summary: Third pharaoh of Egypt's Twentieth Dynasty, who became crown prince after his elder brother's death and ruled about six and a half years from around 1155 BC.

knossos.name: Knossos
knossos.summary: An archaeological site in Crete occupied from the Neolithic period, widely considered Europe's oldest city and the largest centre of the Minoan civilisation; its Palace of Minos was first built around 1900 BC.

hattusa.name: Hattusa
hattusa.summary: Capital of the Hittite Empire in the late Bronze Age, in modern Turkey; its ruins were rediscovered in 1834 and named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

maat.name: Maat
maat.summary: Ancient Egyptian concept and goddess of truth, balance, law and justice, who regulated the stars, seasons and moral order, opposed by chaos.

akhenaten.name: Akhenaten
akhenaten.summary: An ancient Egyptian pharaoh who reigned around 1353 to 1336 BC and abandoned traditional polytheism to introduce worship centered on the sun god Aten, a change reversed after his death.

aten.name: Aten
aten.summary: Ancient Egyptian sun-disc deity that became the sole focus of state worship under pharaoh Akhenaten during the Amarna Period, roughly 1353 to 1336 BCE.

amun.name: Amun
amun.summary: A major ancient Egyptian deity who rose to become patron god of Thebes and, merged with the sun god Ra as Amun-Ra, was worshipped as king of the gods in the New Kingdom.

john-baines-egyptologist.name: John Baines
john-baines-egyptologist.summary: British Egyptologist who was a Professor of Egyptology at the University of Oxford from 1976 to 2013.

atenism.name: Atenism
atenism.summary: Religious system founded by pharaoh Akhenaten centered on worship of the sun god Aten; it was Egypt's state religion for about 20 years before being reversed after his death.

shu-god.name: Shu
shu-god.summary: A primordial Egyptian god of light, air, peace and lions, spouse and brother of the goddess Tefnut and one of the nine deities of the Heliopolis Ennead.

jan-assmann.name: Jan Assmann
jan-assmann.summary: German Egyptologist, cultural historian and religion scholar (1938–2024).

heliopolis-ancient-egypt.name: Heliopolis
heliopolis-ancient-egypt.summary: A major ancient Egyptian city and religious center near modern Cairo, capital of its nome and one of Egypt's oldest cities, now mostly ruined.

atum.name: Atum
atum.summary: Primordial creator god in Egyptian mythology, associated with the evening sun, worshiped from before recorded history through the New Kingdom.

ennead.name: Ennead
ennead.summary: Group of nine deities worshipped at Heliopolis in Egyptian mythology, including Atum, Osiris, Isis and Set, placed under the supremacy of Ra-Atum.

amarna-period.name: Amarna Period
amarna-period.summary: The era of Egyptian history when Pharaoh Akhenaten (1353-1336 BC) moved the capital from Thebes to Akhetaten and promoted worship of the sun disc Aten above other gods.

instruction-of-any.name: The Teaching of Ani
instruction-of-any.summary: An ancient Egyptian wisdom text likely composed in the Eighteenth Dynasty of the New Kingdom, considered difficult and at times obscure to translate due to gaps and corruption in the surviving copy.

the-satire-of-the-trades.name: The Satire of the Trades
the-satire-of-the-trades.summary: Ancient Egyptian instructional text, also called The Instruction of Kheti, praising the scribe's profession over the hardships of other trades.

ahhotep-i.name: Ahhotep I
ahhotep-i.summary: An ancient Egyptian queen who lived around 1560 to 1530 BCE and likely governed as regent for her son Ahmose I; a Karnak stela praises her leadership.

trundholm-sun-chariot.name: Trundholm sun chariot
trundholm-sun-chariot.summary: A Nordic Bronze Age bronze statue of a horse pulling a large disc on wheels, discovered in Denmark in 1902 and now held at the National Museum of Denmark.

orly-goldwasser.name: Orly Goldwasser
orly-goldwasser.summary: Israeli Egyptologist and professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, known for her work on hieroglyphic script and the origin of the alphabet.

apepi.name: Apepi (Apophis)
apepi.summary: A Hyksos ruler of Lower Egypt who reigned about forty years in the early 16th century BC and, in practice, dominated most of Egypt for part of his rule.

pan-grave-culture.name: Pan-Grave culture
pan-grave-culture.summary: A Middle Bronze Age culture of Egypt and Nubia, about 1850 to 1600 BCE, once linked to the Medjay and named for its shallow, pan-shaped graves.

naqada-iii.name: Naqada III
naqada-iii.summary: The final Predynastic phase of Egypt, roughly 3325–3000 BC, also called the Protodynastic Period, when named kings and state formation became visible ahead of Egypt's first dynasty.

jebel-barkal.name: Jebel Barkal
jebel-barkal.summary: A flat-topped mesa near the Nile in Nubia, Sudan, with religious significance for both ancient Kush and ancient Egypt; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003.

napata.name: Napata
napata.summary: An ancient city of Kush near the Nile's fourth cataract, home to a major Amun cult centre and sometime capital of the Kushite kingdom before Meroë took over in 593 BC.

sed-festival.name: Sed festival
sed-festival.summary: An ancient Egyptian ceremony celebrating a pharaoh's continued rule, typically held after thirty years on the throne and then every three to four years, involving processions and religious rites.

aniba-nubia.name: Aniba
aniba-nubia.summary: An ancient Nubian town, known as Miam, about 230 km south of Aswan; inhabited from around 3000 BC, it grew under Egyptian rule during the Middle and New Kingdoms and is now flooded by Lake Nasser.

horus.name: Horus
horus.summary: Ancient Egyptian falcon-headed deity of kingship, healing, protection, the sun and sky, worshipped from prehistoric Egypt into Roman times and linked to the pharaoh as his living manifestation.

mostagedda.name: Mostagedda
mostagedda.summary: Archaeological site and necropolis in Upper Egypt spanning predynastic to Greco-Roman times, including burials of the Nubian Pan-Grave culture.

indus-valley-civilisation.name: Indus Valley Civilisation
indus-valley-civilisation.summary: A Bronze Age civilisation of South Asia lasting from about 3300 to 1300 BCE, one of four great centres of the ancient world alongside Egypt, Mesopotamia and China, known through sites like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
